IN CAPVT PRIMVM
PROBLEMA I.

l.i: An uno & eodem modo aliquid dicatur perfectum

main_text.l: IN genere quidem aliquid dicitur perfectum, cui nihil
deest perfectionis; Imperfectum vero, cui aliquid de-
est. At in specie aliquid dicitur perfectum vel imperfectum,
non uno & eodem, sed variis ac diuersis modis.
Nam 1, aliquid dicitur vel absolute & summe perfectum
sine vlla limitatione, ut ens increatum; vel secundum
quid, seu cum certa limitatione, ut ens creatum. 2, aliquid
dicitur vel simpliciter perfectum, quod in suo ge-nere,

marginalia.note: Perfectum & imperfectum aliquid dicitur variis modis.

page.notes: Left margin notes: the running note "Perfectum & imperfectum aliquid dicitur variis modis." is placed at the start of the paragraph; the section numerals "I." and "II." beside the paragraph are not placed in the XML because their exact line positions are uncertain. They are printed beside "Nam 1" and "2, aliquid" respectively. Thesis 26 reads "Estque" in the scan; the first letter is partly unclear, so it may be "Estque" or similar. The thesis numbers 12–28 are printed as plain numbers; they are given as paragraphs in accordance with the rules. The heading "PROBLEMA I." is a level 2 part; the italic question below it is a level 3 subheading. The page continues in the next column with "nere," and the line ends with the printed hyphen "ge-".
